Select representative texts for each topic

Source: R/inference.R
representatives.Rd

representatives() selects representative texts for each topic of a fitted model: it ranks the units of each topic and returns the first n. A topic in an embedding model is a region of meaning, and it is read most directly from the texts it contains.

Each unit is assigned to the topic whose unit-length center has the highest cosine similarity with it. The texts closest to a topic's center are typical of it but tend to be long, because long texts resemble the average of many texts; texts that are clearly about one topic and no other are usually more telling. With rank = "margin", the default, units are ranked by their margin: the cosine distance to the second-nearest center minus the distance to their own. With rank = "distance" they are ranked by closeness to their own center. Ties go to the shorter text; repeated texts and texts without a word of two or more letters are skipped. By default the units the model was fitted on are ranked, from their stored embeddings; given text, any candidate texts are. The result is a data frame with one row per selected text, ordered by topic and rank.

Because the assignment uses cosine similarity to the unit-length centers, while topics() fits Lloyd's k-means (squared Euclidean distance to the raw means of the normalized embeddings), a few fitted units on topic boundaries can be ranked under a different topic from the one they were fitted to. The representatives stored at fitting time, shown by as.data.frame(fit, what = "representatives"), are the units of each fitted topic closest to its center. For topic words use terms() or keywords().

Usage

representatives(
  object,
  text = NULL,
  model = NULL,
  embeddings = NULL,
  n = 3L,
  rank = c("margin", "distance"),
  batch_size = 32L
)

Arguments

object

A fitted model from topics().

text

Character vector of candidate texts, or NULL (default) for the documents or segments the model was fitted on.

model

A model from load_model(), a pinned model name, or NULL (default) for the default model, used to embed text; ignored when embeddings are given.

embeddings

Numeric matrix with one row per candidate, or NULL (default): the stored embeddings when text is NULL, else encode text.

n

Number of texts per topic (default 3).

rank

"margin" (default) or "distance".

batch_size

Texts per model call when encoding (default 32).

Value

A base data frame with one row per selected text and columns topic, rank, text, distance (cosine distance to the unit's own center), and margin, ordered by topic and rank. When the fitted units are ranked, document_id (and segment, for a segmented model) follow rank. Topics without units have no rows.

Conditions

sbert_no_embeddings when text is NULL and the model stores no embeddings; sbert_dimension_mismatch when the embeddings have a different number of columns from the fitted model; sbert_bad_input when both model and embeddings are given or embeddings has the wrong number of rows; when encoding, the conditions of encode().

See also

terms() and keywords() for topic words; name_topics() to label topics; plot(fit, type = "representatives") to draw them; topic_membership() for graded membership.

Examples

corpus <- head(dedupe(feedback_translations, column = "translation"), 600)
topic_model <- topics(corpus, n_topics = 6, column = "translation",
                      embeddings = feedback_embeddings)
representatives(topic_model, n = 2)

# Rank new candidate texts, giving their embeddings.
text <- c(
  "Cats chase mice", "Dogs chase balls",
  "Stocks and bonds trade", "Markets price shares"
)
embeddings <- rbind(c(1, 0), c(0.9, 0.1), c(0, 1), c(0.1, 0.9))
toy_model <- topics(text, 2, embeddings = embeddings)
representatives(
  toy_model,
  c("kittens pounce", "bond yields", "pets and prices"),
  embeddings = rbind(c(1, 0.1), c(0.1, 1), c(0.7, 0.7)),
  n = 1
)
#>   topic rank           text     distance    margin
#> 1     1    1 kittens pounce 0.0009828586 0.8446397
#> 2     2    1    bond yields 0.0009828586 0.8446397
